classification.classification_note: The bug is a read of an uninitialized stack `blst_fp` object. The top-level MSAN report is triggered by `blst_fp_sqrt(&result, &A)` inside the `IsSquare(A)` assertion, after the same case has already read `A` via `blst_fp_is_square(&A)` without first loading `op.bn0` into `A`.

bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5684624024535040 Project: bls-signatures Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer Fuzz Target: cryptofuzz-bls-signatures_optimize_size Job Type: libfuzzer_msan_bls-signatures Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value Crash State: cryptofuzz::module::blst_detail::OpBignumCalc_prime / cryptofuzz::module::blst::OpBignumCalc / cryptofuzz::ExecutorBignumCalc::callModule Sanitizer: memory (MSAN).
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source snapshot / _work/src/build.sh / patch.diff
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the saved issue for the exact staged witness `poc` (68 bytes, sha256 `628c4041ebb13b22cc048480be30451cc99c2118f137a506801dc8afd9e05837`), but the rebuilt vulnerable workspace lost sanitizer fidelity and only emitted a raw SIGSEGV; `sanitizer_trace.txt` is therefore the authoritative runtime evidence. Decoding that witness with cryptofuzz's datasource rules yields outer operation `BignumCalc_Mod_BLS12_381_P`, a 31-byte inner payload, an empty modifier, raw outer module selector `0x2020202020202020`, and `continue=false`; decoding the inner payload yields `calcOp = IsSquare(A)`. The saved target build script rewrites `extra_options.h` with `--force-module=blst`, `entry.cpp` feeds that option into `Options`, and `ExecutorBase::getModule` overwrites the raw module selector before lookup, so the exact witness still reaches the loaded blst module. The modular executor injects the hard-coded BLS12-381 prime into `op.modulo`, so `blst::OpBignumCalc` takes the `OpBignumCalc_prime(op)` helper. That helper declares stack locals `blst_fp result, A, B;`, leaving `A` uninitialized. In the `IsSquare(A)` case, unlike neighboring prime-field cases such as `Sqrt(A)` and `Not(A)`, no `CF_CHECK_TRUE(blst_detail::To_blst_fp(op.bn0, A));` runs before `A` is used. The case first derives `is_square` from `blst_fp_is_square(&A)`, then calls `blst_fp_sqrt(&result, &A)` inside `CF_ASSERT(...)`; the saved MSAN trace reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `cryptofuzz/modules/blst/module.cpp:1187:21` and attributes the origin to local `A` from this function's stack frame. The supplied `patch.diff` is unrelated to this path and only bumps the exported MCL version constant.

source.description: First project-code parse of the attacker-controlled request type. This outer operation ID determines which BignumCalc executor runs and therefore which fixed modulo, if any, is attached to the operation object.
source.value_from: Decoding the exact 68-byte witness in `poc` (sha256 `628c4041ebb13b22cc048480be30451cc99c2118f137a506801dc8afd9e05837`) with cryptofuzz's datasource rules yields `operation = CF_OPERATION("BignumCalc_Mod_BLS12_381_P")`, a 31-byte payload, empty modifier, raw module selector `0x2020202020202020`, and `continue=false`. `_work/src/build.sh` bakes `--force-module=blst` into this target, so `getModule` overwrites that raw selector; the outer operation still uniquely selects the executor that later injects the BLS12-381 prime constant matched by `blst::OpBignumCalc`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The prime-field helper allocates stack slot `A` without an initializer. The authoritative MSAN origin reports the uninitialized value was created by the allocation of `A` in this stack frame (reported at function line 1077).

sink.description: MSAN crash site. The `IsSquare(A)` assertion recomputes `blst_fp_sqrt` on stack object `A` even though this case never initialized `A` from `op.bn0`.
sink.note: The saved authoritative `sanitizer_trace.txt` reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/cryptofuzz/modules/blst/module.cpp:1187:21` in `cryptofuzz::module::blst_detail::OpBignumCalc_prime`, and the origin stack identifies the uninitialized object as local `A` from this same function.

root_cause.description: Root cause. This prime-field case reaches `blst_fp_is_square(&A)` and `blst_fp_sqrt(&result, &A)` without the `CF_CHECK_TRUE(blst_detail::To_blst_fp(op.bn0, A));` initialization present in neighboring `A`-consuming cases such as `Sqrt(A)`, `Not(A)`, `Set(A)`, `IsEq(A,B)`, and `IsZero(A)`.
root_cause.note: The provided `patch.diff` does not touch this path; it only bumps `include/mcl/op.hpp` from version `0x153` to `0x154`. The missing initialization obligation is therefore established directly from the staged vulnerable source and the saved MSAN origin/sink trace, not from the supplied patch artifact.

parser_admitted.description: The saved build script's `--operations=` allowlist includes `BignumCalc_Mod_BLS12_381_P`, so the outer operation ID parsed at line 109 survives the line-111 filter and reaches this driver arm, which hands the 31-byte request payload to the modular BLS12-381-prime executor.

forced_module_selected.description: The saved target build script writes `--force-module=blst` into `extra_options.h`; `entry.cpp` feeds that string into `Options`, so `getModule` overwrites the witness's raw selector `0x2020202020202020` with the loaded blst module ID before `ExecutorBase::Run` reaches `callModule`.

prime_helper_selected.description: Because the forced module is blst and the selected executor injected the BLS12-381 prime modulus into `op.modulo`, `blst::OpBignumCalc` dispatches to `blst_detail::OpBignumCalc_prime(op)` instead of the order-field helper or returning `std::nullopt`.

evidence_limitations: Stage 01 rebuilt the vulnerable workspace and reproduced only a raw `SIGSEGV` (`returncode 139`). The authoritative runtime evidence for this GT is therefore the staged `sanitizer_trace.txt` / `default_crash_trace.txt`, which preserve the original MemorySanitizer stack and origin information.

The supplied `patch.diff` is unrelated to the crashing path: it only changes the exported MCL version constant and does not modify `cryptofuzz/modules/blst/module.cpp`. No matching fix hunk or local git history is available in the staged non-git workspace, so the root cause is grounded directly from the vulnerable source and the saved MSAN trace.

The staged source tree now contains an empty checked-in `cryptofuzz/extra_options.h`; the forced-module behavior used here is grounded from the saved `_work/src/build.sh` that regenerates that header during compilation, together with `cryptofuzz/entry.cpp`, `cryptofuzz/options.cpp`, and `cryptofuzz/executor.cpp` that consume the option.

coarse_trace.summary: cryptofuzz parses the outer request type and dispatches the witness into the `BignumCalc_Mod_BLS12_381_P` executor.

The modular BignumCalc parser materializes the inner `calcOp`, the selected executor injects the hard-coded BLS12-381 prime modulus into `op.modulo`, and the target's forced-module setting makes `getModule` hand the operation to blst.
The blst module matches that modulus, enters the prime-field helper, and allocates stack locals `result`, `A`, and `B` without initializing `A`.
Inside `case CF_CALCOP("IsSquare(A)")`, the prime-field helper omits the usual `To_blst_fp(op.bn0, A)` initialization and first derives `is_square` from uninitialized `A`.
The assertion recomputes `blst_fp_sqrt(&result, &A)` on the same uninitialized `A`, and MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `module.cpp:1187`.

fine_trace.note: Source. `Driver::Run` consumes the first request selector from the attacker-controlled datasource. On the exact witness, this field decodes to `CF_OPERATION("BignumCalc_Mod_BLS12_381_P")`.

Because the saved target build allowlist includes this operation, the outer selector survives the line-111 `options.operations` filter, takes the `BignumCalc_Mod_BLS12_381_P` switch arm, and forwards the 31-byte payload into that executor. The remaining outer datasource bytes stay available for modifier, module-selection, and loop-control parsing inside `ExecutorBase::Run`.

Within the BignumCalc payload parser, the first field materialized is the inner arithmetic selector `calcOp` (delegating to `Type::Type(ds)` / `ds.Get<uint64_t>(0)`). On the exact witness, it decodes to `CF_CALCOP("IsSquare(A)")`.
The selected modular executor injects its hard-coded BLS12-381 prime decimal string into `op.modulo`. That exact constant is what the blst module later matches to choose the prime-field helper.

The saved target build writes `--force-module=blst` into `extra_options.h`; `entry.cpp` and `options.cpp` turn that into `options.forceModule`, so `getModule` overwrites the witness's raw outer selector `0x2020202020202020` and returns the loaded blst module. This is the source-grounded bridge from the exact witness to `callModule`.

Once `callModule` targets the forced blst module, `blst::OpBignumCalc` sees `op.modulo` equal to the BLS12-381 prime and dispatches into `OpBignumCalc_prime(op)` instead of the order-field helper or `std::nullopt`.

Upon entering the prime-field helper, stack locals `result`, `A`, and `B` are declared without initializers. MSAN's origin identifies this stack slot `A` as the uninitialized object that later reaches the sink.

Root cause. The inner `calcOp` selects `IsSquare(A)`, but unlike `Sqrt(A)` just above and the later `Not(A)`, `Set(A)`, `IsEq(A,B)`, and `IsZero(A)` cases, this arm has no `CF_CHECK_TRUE(blst_detail::To_blst_fp(op.bn0, A));`. Control therefore enters the case body with `A` still in the declaration-state bytes from step 7.

The case's first statement derives boolean `is_square` by reading `A` through `blst_fp_is_square(&A)`. This materializes a downstream value from indeterminate field-element bytes and supplies the left-hand side of the later assertion.

Sink. The assertion recomputes `blst_fp_sqrt(&result, &A)` on the same uninitialized `A` and compares it against `is_square`. The saved MSAN trace reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at this line (`1187:21`) and attributes the origin to local `A` from step 7.

allocation_context.note: The saved MSAN trace says: `Uninitialized value was created by an allocation of 'A' in the stack frame of function '_ZN10cryptofuzz6module11blst_detail18OpBignumCalc_primeERNS_9operation10BignumCalcE'` at `module.cpp:1077`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Allocation context identifies the uninitialized stack slot `A`; root cause is the later `IsSquare(A)` case that uses that slot without calling `To_blst_fp(op.bn0, A)`.

poc.trigger: The exact staged 68-byte witness `poc` decodes as outer operation `BignumCalc_Mod_BLS12_381_P`, inner `calcOp` `IsSquare(A)`, empty modifier, raw module selector `0x2020202020202020`, and `continue=false`. This target's saved build script forces `getModule` to `blst`, so the witness reaches `cryptofuzz::module::blst_detail::OpBignumCalc_prime`; the authoritative `sanitizer_trace.txt` then records `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `module.cpp:1187:21` with the stack `OpBignumCalc_prime -> blst::OpBignumCalc -> ExecutorBignumCalc::callModule`. The rebuilt vulnerable run preserved crash/no-crash behavior but lost sanitizer fidelity and only emitted raw SIGSEGV, so the staged MSAN trace is the authoritative runtime evidence for this GT.

format.name: cryptofuzz modular BignumCalc corpus input
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact 68-byte witness in `poc` (sha256 `628c4041ebb13b22cc048480be30451cc99c2118f137a506801dc8afd9e05837`). Under cryptofuzz's datasource format it must continue to decode as outer operation `BignumCalc_Mod_BLS12_381_P`, a 31-byte payload whose inner `calcOp` is `IsSquare(A)`, an empty modifier, raw outer module selector `0x2020202020202020`, and `continue=false`. The raw module selector need not name a valid module for this target because `_work/src/build.sh` bakes `--force-module=blst`, and `ExecutorBase::getModule` overwrites that field before lookup. After the forced blst selection, the modular executor must inject the BLS12-381 prime so `blst::OpBignumCalc` dispatches into `OpBignumCalc_prime`'s `IsSquare(A)` arm. The crash does not rely on any arithmetic property of the parsed bignums; it happens because this case skips `To_blst_fp(op.bn0, A)` altogether. This GT does not generalize beyond that exact witnessed corpus semantics.
